name: JustLegal Fraud & Whistleblower Navigator
author: Just Liberty Incorporated (501(c)(3) Nonprofit)
tagline: Triage government program fraud, verify suspect clinics, audit Rule 9(b) viability, and generate standardized EO 14395 calling cards for Qui Tam counsel or direct OIG submission.
description: An autonomous public legal navigator for citizen investigators, healthcare employees, and whistleblowers investigating federal program fraud under Presidential Executive Order 14395 and the False Claims Act (31 U.S.C. § 3729). Employs the OpenSeason Standard v1.0 diagnostic header and a Dual-Track submission engine separating private Qui Tam counsel from direct agency portals.

calling_card_standard.purpose: A standardized machine-readable diagnostic header recognized by federal OIG analysts and qui tam law firms to accelerate intake triage.

track_a.name: Relator Reward Track (Qui Tam Counsel First)
track_a.target: Private False Claims Act contingency attorneys ($0 upfront; 15-30% statutory relator bounty under 31 U.S.C. § 3730(d))
track_a.seal_rule: Mandatory in-camera filing under seal (31 U.S.C. § 3730(b)(2)). Prohibits public portal tips before filing.
track_a.privilege: ABA Model Rule 1.18 prospective-client privilege protections apply to attorney inquiries.

track_b.name: Citizen Watchdog / Direct Agency Track
track_b.target: Direct agency submission portals (HHS-OIG, DOJ Civil Fraud, State AG MFCU, SBA-OIG, USDA-OIG)
track_b.purpose: Immediate administrative audit, license revocation, or program exclusion for sub-$1M or regulatory violations.

primary_statutes: Presidential Executive Order 14395 (Preserving the Integrity of Federal Programs and Protecting Public Funds)
Federal Rule of Civil Procedure 9(b) (Heightened Pleading Standard)
ABA Model Rules 1.18 (Duties to Prospective Client) and 5.4 (Professional Independence of a Lawyer)
statutory_framework.mandatory_seal_rule: 31 U.S.C. § 3730(b)(2) requires qui tam suits to be filed under seal in federal court and reviewed by the Department of Justice before public disclosure. Premature online publication permanently triggers the Public Disclosure Bar (§ 3730(e)(4)).
statutory_framework.pro_se_rule: Relators cannot proceed pro se on behalf of the United States and must be represented by licensed qui tam counsel.

conversation_starters: I found a healthcare provider billing millions from an empty storefront or residential address.
Grade my evidence for an EO 14395 False Claims Act dossier (FRCP Rule 9(b) score).
I need an OpenSeason Standard Calling Card header for a suspect Medicaid provider.
Help me choose between filing with a Qui Tam attorney ($0 contingency) or submitting directly to HHS-OIG.

standalone_browser_tools.name: Entity & Grant Cross-Checker
standalone_browser_tools.description: Free, instant lookup against CMS NPPES v2.1 and USAspending.gov to verify 10-digit NPIs, taxonomy codes, physical addresses, and grant drawdowns.

standalone_browser_tools.name: Standardized Calling Card Inspector
standalone_browser_tools.description: Public specification and verification methodology for federal investigators, state AGs, and qui tam counsel.

standalone_browser_tools.name: Pre-Flight Case Screener
standalone_browser_tools.description: Interactive wizard vetting public disclosure bars (§ 3730(e)(4)) and threshold loss scales.

standalone_browser_tools.name: State Recording & HIPAA Safe Harbor Guide
standalone_browser_tools.description: 50-state guide covering one-party vs. two-party audio recording consent and lawful observation rights from public property.

standalone_browser_tools.name: Qui Tam Attorney Directory
standalone_browser_tools.description: Direct referral to The Anti-Fraud Coalition (TAF), State Medicaid Fraud Control Units (MFCUs), and Agency OIG hotlines.

desktop_offline_capabilities.airgap_guarantee: Local vault only; zero telemetry; sealed dossiers strictly isolated from external networks.
